title: SharedAddition
description: One thing a linked device added, as the others receive it: what it is called and every identifier and host it goes by — never a token. Each device publishes to a ring of its own under furlough.adds.<id>, holding at most the last 20.

id.description: The sender's target id. A second write about the same thing — its first rule landing — replaces the first in the ring rather than sitting beside it.

sequence.description: One higher on every write from this sender. Per sender, never compared across senders; what the receiver's watermark counts.

title.description: What to call it: "YouTube", or the host when nothing better is known.

isApp.description: Whether the sender's face was an app. A phone receiving one cannot add the app itself and says so; a Mac looks for it among what is installed.

bundleIDs.description: Lowercased bundle identifiers it is known by, on either platform. May be empty.

hosts.description: The hosts the sender actually blocks for it. May be empty.

rule.description: The sender's rule, if it had one yet. Applied on arrival only where the receiver's row has none — a rule of your own is never overwritten by a device you are not holding.

half.description: Where it was added: the everyday rules, or the anchor's list.

origin.description: The sending device's id, equal to the <id> in the ring's key. What the receiver's watermark is keyed by.

addedAt.description: When it was sent. Receivers take unseen additions in this order, oldest first.

rule.title: Rule
rule.description: When a target may be used, and for how many minutes a day in total. Travels only as a passenger on an addition; there is no rule sync.

windows.description: The allowed spans. Absent or empty means open all day, every day: only the budget limits it. Once there are any, a day none of them covers is blocked.

dailyBudgetMinutes.description: Minutes a day in total. A whole day of budget (1440) is no budget at all.

budgetByWeekday.description: Seven minute counts, Sunday first, when the week is not one number. Anything but exactly seven entries decodes as absent: the safe reading of a damaged field is the rule's one budget, never a day left without one.

timeWindow.title: TimeWindow
timeWindow.description: A span of minutes inside one calendar day, on the days of the week it applies. A stored span never crosses midnight: an evening that runs late is an evening window plus an early-morning window whose days are shifted one day on.

days.description: Days of the week as a bit set, bit 0 Sunday, so bits line up with Calendar's weekday numbers 1…7. Absent means every day (127).
